title: Simple Past: Regular and Irregular Verbs / Pasado simple: verbos regulares e irregulares
bridge: Na Spanish, nke a na-eme ka ndoro ndoro dị n'ụzọ na-egosi nke gara aga (hablé, comí, viví). Na Igbo, ndoro ndoro nke nwere -ed (talk → talked), mana ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro (go → went). N'ime ha, na Igbo, nke a na-eme ka ndoro ndoro dị n'ụzọ na-egosi nke gara aga (I went, you went, he went), mana na Spanish, o na-egosi nke gara aga (fui, fuiste, fue). Kedu ka ị na-eme ka ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro!
rule: Nke a na-eme ka ndoro ndoro dị n'ụzọ na-egosi nke gara aga na nke gara aga. Na ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro, ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro -ed (work → worked, play → played). Mgbe ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro 'e', ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro -d (live → lived); mgbe ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro 'y', ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro 'y' na-eme ka 'i' na-eme ka -ed (study → studied). Ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro (see → saw, eat → ate) ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro. Na ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro 'did' + ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro (I didn't go, Did you see?). Nke a na-eme ka ndoro ndoro dị n'ụzọ na-egosi nke gara aga. Nke a na-eme ka ndoro ndoro dị n'ụzọ na-egosi nke gara aga 'yesterday', 'last week', 'in 2010'.

concept_examples.text: I walked to the park yesterday.
concept_examples.translation: Ahu m bịara ugwu n'ụzọ n'ụtụtụ.

concept_examples.text: She ate an apple for breakfast.
We didn't watch TV last night.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wiː ˈdɪdnt wɑːtʃ tiː ˈviː læst naɪt/

concept_examples.translation: Ị mere ka ọnụ a ga?

common_error.correct_alt: She didn't go to school yesterday.
common_error.explanation: A na-eme ka ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro 'did' (ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro), ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro 'go'. Chọọ ka ị maara: 'did' na-egosi nke gara aga, mana ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro.

examples.original: I played football last Sunday.
examples.translation: Ahu m jụrụ ọkụkọ n'izuọchị asaa gara aga.
examples.note: Nwere -ed na ndoro ndoro 'play' na-eme ka 'played'.

examples.original: She studied for the exam.
examples.translation: Ọ zụrụ ihe n'okpuru ụzọ gara aga.
examples.note: Mgbe ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro 'y', ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro 'y' na-eme ka 'i' na-eme ka -ed: study → studied.

examples.original: We lived in Madrid for two years.
examples.phonetic: /wiː lɪvd ɪn məˈdrɪd fər tuː jɪrz/
examples.translation: Anyị nwere mmadụ n'ụlọ nke abụọ afọ gara aga.
examples.note: Ndoro ndoro 'live' na-eme ka 'lived'.

examples.original: I went to the cinema with my friends.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ went tə ðə ˈsɪnəmə wɪð maɪ frendz/
examples.translation: Ahu m gaa ugwu n'ụlọ ọrịa na ndị m.
examples.note: 'Go' na-eme ka 'went'. Chọọ ka ị maara ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro (go-went, see-saw, eat-ate).

examples.original: She saw a beautiful bird in the tree.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː sɔː ə ˈbjuːtɪfl bɜːrd ɪn ðə triː/
examples.translation: Ọ huu nwoke ọma n'okpuru ụzọ.
examples.note: 'See' na-eme ka 'saw'. Ọ bụghị 'seed'.

examples.original: He ate all the cookies.
examples.translation: Ọ rịrị okpa nkwụ nke ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: 'Eat' na-eme ka 'ate'. Nke a na-eme ka 'eɪt', a na-eme ka 'iːt'.

levels.label: Negatives and Questions
levels.translation: Ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro

examples.original: I didn't like the movie.
examples.translation: Enweghi m nwere ike ịmụta ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: Na ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro 'didn't' + ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro. Ndoro ndoro 'like' enweghi ike ịmụta.

examples.original: Did you finish your homework?
examples.translation: Ị mere ka ị nwere ike ịmụta?
examples.note: Na ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro 'Did' + ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro. Enweghi ike ịmụta na ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro.

examples.original: They didn't come to the party.
examples.translation: Ha enweghi ike ịbanye n'ụlọ ọrịa.
examples.note: Chọọ ka ị maara: 'come' na-eme ka 'came', mana na ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro 'come', a na-eme ka 'came'.

title: Present Progressive (Presente Continuo)
bridge: N'igbo, nke a na-egosi na nke a na-eme n'oge zuru ezu maobu n'oge ndoro nke eme. N'igbo, anyị na-eme nke a na-egosi na nke a na-eme n'oge zuru ezu maobu n'oge ndoro nke eme. N'ihi na ndoro ndoro ndoro, ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro. N'ihi na ndoro ndoro ndoro, ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro.
rule: Nke a na-egosi na nke a na-eme n'oge zuru ezu maobu n'oge ndoro nke eme. Nke a na-egosi na nke a na-eme n'oge zuru ezu maobu n'oge ndoro nke eme. Nke a na-egosi na nke a na-eme n'oge zuru ezu maobu n'oge ndoro nke eme. Nke a na-egosi na nke a na-eme n'oge zuru ezu maobu n'oge ndoro nke eme. Nke a na-egosi na nke a na-eme n'oge zuru ezu maobu n'oge ndoro nke eme.

concept_examples.translation: O na-eme ajuju n'ogbe na Madrid.

common_error.explanation: Nke a na-egosi na nke a na-eme n'oge zuru ezu maobu n'oge ndoro nke eme. Nke a na-egosi na nke a na-eme n'oge zuru ezu maobu n'oge ndoro nke eme. Nke a na-egosi na nke a na-eme n'oge zuru ezu maobu n'oge ndoro nke eme.

levels.label: Forming the Present Continuous
levels.translation: Nke a na-egosi na nke a na-eme n'oge zuru ezu maobu n'oge ndoro nke eme

examples.original: I am eating.
examples.translation: A na-eme nri.
examples.note: Use 'am' na 'I'.

examples.original: He is running.
examples.translation: O na-eme igba egwuregwu.
examples.note: Use 'is' na 'he', 'she', 'it'.

examples.original: They are playing football.
examples.translation: Ha na-eme football.
examples.note: Use 'are' na 'you', 'we', 'they'.

examples.original: We are watching TV.
examples.translation: Anyi na-eme n'ulo television.
examples.note: Remember to change 'y' to 'i' and add -ing (watch > watching).

levels.label: Negatives and Questions
levels.translation: Nke a na-egosi na nke a na-eme n'oge zuru ezu maobu n'oge ndoro nke eme

examples.original: I am not sleeping.
examples.translation: A amaghị ime nri.
examples.note: The negation is formed with 'am not', 'is not', 'are not'.

examples.original: She is not crying.
examples.translation: O amaghị ime n'anya.
examples.note: Common contraction: isn't.

examples.original: Are you studying?
examples.translation: I na-eme igbo?
examples.note: Invert the subject and auxiliary to ask.

examples.original: What is he doing?
examples.translation: Kedu na-eme ya?
examples.note: Wh- questions have the auxiliary after the question word.

levels.label: Use and Exceptions
levels.translation: Nke a na-egosi na nke a na-eme n'oge zuru ezu maobu n'oge ndoro nke eme

examples.original: He is working in London these days.
examples.phonetic: /hiː ɪz ˈwɜːkɪŋ ɪn ˈlʌndən ðiːz deɪz/
examples.translation: O na-eme ajuju n'ogbe na London ugbu a.
examples.note: Used for temporary actions, not habitual ones.

examples.original: We are going to the cinema tomorrow.
examples.phonetic: /wiː ɑːr ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə ðə ˈsɪnəmə təˈmɒrəʊ/
examples.translation: Anyi ga-enye cinema n'izu ugbu a.
examples.note: Used for future plans.

examples.original: I like this song.
examples.translation: Ahu mma m nke a tụlụ.
examples.note: Don't say 'I am liking' because 'like' is a stative verb.

examples.original: She doesn't want to go.
examples.translation: O amaghị ị ga enye.
examples.note: Use the simple present with stative verbs like want, know, prefer.

title: Future with going to / Nzukọ ụzọ ọma nwere ike ịbanye n'oge mbụ
bridge: N'SPANISH, tụọrọ ụzọ ịtụle ụbọchị ụzọ dị mma ka o si bụrụ na a na-egosi ụbọchị mbụ n'ụtụtụ (n'ụtụtụ m ga-eje ozi n'ụlọ ọrụ). N'igbo, ụzọ ọma nwere ike ịbanye n'oge mbụ bụ nzukọ ụzọ dị mma nwere ike ịbanye n'oge mbụ n'igbo. N'igbo, tụọrọ ụzọ ịtụle ụbọchị ụzọ dị mma ka o si bụrụ na a na-egosi ụbọchị mbụ n'ụtụtụ (n'ụtụtụ m ga-eje ozi n'ụlọ ọrụ). N'igbo, tụọrọ ụzọ ịtụle ụbọchị ụzọ dị mma ka o si bụrụ na a na-egosi ụbọchị mbụ n'ụtụtụ (n'ụtụtụ m ga-eje ozi n'ụlọ ọrụ).
rule: I nzukọ ụzọ ịtụle ụbọchị ụzọ dị mma ka o si bụrụ na a na-egosi ụbọchị mbụ n'ụtụtụ (n'ụtụtụ m ga-eje ozi n'ụlọ ọrụ), tụọrọ ụzọ ịtụle ụbọchị ụzọ dị mma ka o si bụrụ na a na-egosi ụbọchị mbụ n'ụtụtụ (n'ụtụtụ m ga-eje ozi n'ụlọ ọrụ). N'igbo, tụọrọ ụzọ ịtụle ụbọchị ụzọ dị mma ka o si bụrụ na a na-egosi ụbọchị mbụ n'ụtụtụ (n'ụtụtụ m ga-eje ozi n'ụlọ ọrụ).

concept_examples.text: I am going to visit my grandmother tomorrow.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ æm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə ˈvɪzɪt maɪ ˈɡrændˌmʌðər təˈmɑːroʊ/

concept_examples.text: She is going to buy a new car.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ na-achọ ịzụ ndụ ụgbọ ala ọhụrụ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃiː ɪz ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə baɪ ə nuː kɑːr/

concept_examples.text: We are not going to watch TV tonight.

concept_examples.text: Are you going to come to the party?
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɑːr juː ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə kʌm tə ðə ˈpɑːrti/

common_error.wrong: I going to travel next week.
common_error.correct: I am going to travel next week.
common_error.correct_alt: I'm going to travel next week.
common_error.explanation: N'SPANISH, tụọrọ ụzọ ịtụle ụbọchị ụzọ dị mma ka o si bụrụ na a na-egosi ụbọchị mbụ n'ụtụtụ (n'ụtụtụ m ga-eje ozi n'ụlọ ọrụ). N'igbo, tụọrọ ụzọ ịtụle ụbọchị ụzọ dị mma ka o si bụrụ na a na-egosi ụbọchị mbụ n'ụtụtụ (n'ụtụtụ m ga-eje ozi n'ụlọ ọrụ).

levels.label: Affirmative: Plans and Intentions
levels.translation: Akwukwọ ndụ: Ndoro na ike ịbanye n'oge mbụ

examples.original: I am going to study English tonight.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ æm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə ˈstʌdi ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ təˈnaɪt/
examples.translation: A ga-akwụ ụzọ n'ụtụtụ a.
examples.note: Ụzọ ọma nwere ike ịbanye n'oge mbụ n'igbo ka o si bụrụ na a na-egosi ụbọchị mbụ n'ụtụtụ (n'ụtụtụ m ga-eje ozi n'ụlọ ọrụ).

examples.original: They are going to have dinner at a restaurant.

examples.translation: Ha ga-eriri nri n'ụlọ ndụ.
examples.note: Ụzọ ọma nwere ike ịbanye n'oge mbụ n'igbo ka o si bụrụ na a na-egosi ụbọchị mbụ n'ụtụtụ (n'ụtụtụ m ga-eje ozi n'ụlọ ọrụ).

examples.original: He is going to call his boss.

examples.translation: Ọ ga-eme ka ọ zụọ okpukpere ndụ ya.
examples.note: Ụzọ ọma nwere ike ịbanye n'oge mbụ n'igbo ka o si bụrụ na a na-egosi ụbọchị mbụ n'ụtụtụ (n'ụtụtụ m ga-eje ozi n'ụlọ ọrụ).

examples.original: I am not going to eat fast food.

examples.note: Ụzọ ọma nwere ike ịbanye n'oge mbụ n'igbo ka o si bụrụ na a na-egosi ụbọchị mbụ n'ụtụtụ (n'ụtụtụ m ga-eje ozi n'ụlọ ọrụ).

examples.original: Are you going to help me?

examples.note: Ụzọ ọma nwere ike ịbanye n'oge mbụ n'igbo ka o si bụrụ na a na-egosi ụbọchị mbụ n'ụtụtụ (n'ụtụtụ m ga-eje ozi n'ụlọ ọrụ).

levels.label: Predictions with Evidence
levels.translation: Ndoro nwere ike ịbanye n'oge mbụ n'ụzọ doro n'anya

examples.original: The car is going to crash!
examples.translation: Ụgbọ ala ga-achọ ịkpa!.
